objectives.text: Describe the journey of food through the mouth, stomach and intestines, and explain how the lungs fill and empty as we breathe
successCriteria: I can say food is chewed in the mouth, mixed in the stomach, and the good parts are taken out in the intestines
I can explain that the lungs fill with air and grow bigger when we breathe in, then shrink as air flows back out
assessmentPoints: Digestion order answers in the opening activity
Responses when the filling and emptying lungs are followed in the second activity

objectives.text: Trace the loop of blood from the heart to the body and back, and explain why blood is never used up
successCriteria: I can trace one drop of blood from the heart out to the body and back to the heart
I can explain that the heart is a pump and the same blood keeps going round the loop instead of being used up
assessmentPoints: Blood-loop tracing in the third activity
Worksheet and exit ticket answers in the closing practice

activities.title: Digestion: food travels mouth to intestines
Breathing: air moves in and out of the lungs
Circulation: blood loops round and round

differentiation.support: Provide a simple heart-and-body loop diagram with arrows so learners can follow one drop of blood out to the body and back before tracing it themselves.

activities.title: A common mistake: blood is not used up

differentiation.stretch: Ask learners to explain why the returning drop of blood proves the heart does not burn blood up like fuel.
